metadata.source: Certified 2026 Hackensack City Fiscal Baseline & NJ Title 54

coreInequities.title: High Residential Reliance
coreInequities.description: With 68.2% of the property tax levy borne by homeowners, unforeseen municipal or school costs directly inflate residential bills.
coreInequities.remedy: Expand commercial ratables and pursue shared services to mitigate residential exposure.

coreInequities.title: Assessment Base Calibration
coreInequities.description: Hackensack City operates at an equalization ratio of 65.4%, requiring state equalization adjustments for county tax apportionment.
coreInequities.remedy: Continuous annual revaluation adjustments to maintain assessments at 100% true market value.

presetScenarios.name: State Formula Aid & Ratable Equalization
presetScenarios.summary: Achieving full state formula school aid and expanding commercial ratables reduces residential millage.
presetScenarios.winners: Hackensack City residential homeowners and fixed-income seniors.

presetScenarios.name: Countywide Shared Services & Joint Purchasing
presetScenarios.summary: Partnering with Bergen County on joint dispatch, specialized public works equipment, and health benefit pooling.

policyRoadmap.title: Establish Municipal Shared Service Compact
policyRoadmap.description: Formally join Bergen County cooperative purchasing agreements for road resurfacing materials, salt, and emergency dispatch.

policyRoadmap.title: MOD-IV Annual Assessment Roll Calibration
policyRoadmap.description: Maintain certified assessments within 5% of equalized market value to eliminate county tax appeal exposure.
policyRoadmap.impact: Protects against sudden tax appeal refund spikes.
